title: Point Class
summary: Official Derivative Python API reference for Point objects, covering SOP.points access, point index, owner, position AttributeData, coordinate aliases, normalized bounding-box position, dynamic attributes, and scriptSOP point destruction.
guidance: Use this article when generated Python code traverses SOP.points and needs point-level position or attribute access.
Use P for the point coordinates as AttributeData, or x, y, and z as aliases for P[0], P[1], and P[2].
Use normP when a point's normalized position within the SOP bounding box is needed.
Treat geometry attributes as dynamic Point members, such as Point.uv or Point.N, only after confirming the attribute exists.
Do not use Point Class as a POP point iteration API; POP geometry is GPU-oriented and should be handled with POP Class and POP operator cards.
Use destroy() only for points owned by scriptSOP workflows; existing Point objects in the same SOP may become invalid afterward.
